title: Time Period in Simple Harmonic Motion (Spring and Pendulum)

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Oscillations

explanation: For a mass-spring system undergoing SHM, time period depends on mass m and spring constant k, but NOT on amplitude — a stiffer spring (larger k) or smaller mass gives a shorter period (faster oscillation). For a simple pendulum (small-angle approximation, θ < ~10°), time period depends on the pendulum's length L and local gravitational acceleration g, but NOT on the mass of the bob or the amplitude of swing (for small angles) — this independence from amplitude is the defining feature of isochronism in SHM.

workedExample.scenario: A simple pendulum of length 1 m on Earth (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²).

commonMistakes: Assuming a heavier pendulum bob swings slower — pendulum time period is independent of the bob's mass entirely.
Applying the simple pendulum formula for large swing angles — the T = 2π√(L/g) formula is only accurate for the small-angle approximation (typically under about 10°).
genZNote: Pendulum period doesn't care about the bob's mass — length and gravity are the only ones calling the shots.
